title: Observability: token + KV metrics, tracing, logging, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Reduce alert noise and improve root-cause time for token-level and KV-cache related regressions by adding fine-grained metrics, tracing spans, structured logging context, updated Grafana dashboards, and tuned alert rules. This PR introduces new Prometheus metrics for per-request token cost and latency, KV-cache hit/miss counters and latencies, enriched tracing spans that propagate model_id and route tags, and structured logs for sampling/debugging hot paths. Dashboards: new panels for token-cost breakdown by model/route, KV-cache hit-rate and latency heatmaps, and an overview page with SLO-oriented panels. Alerts: thresholds reworked to use rate-aggregation and burn-rate windows, added suppression for expected cold-start spikes, and split high-cardinality alerts into route-level and system-level rules. Testing: unit tests for metrics instrumentation, integration tests exercising end-to-end telemetry with a test Prometheus + Jaeger stack, and dashboard JSON schema validation. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics exporter changes and backfills - [x] Add traces and baggage for model/route - [x] Update Grafana dashboard JSONs and docs - [x] Implement alert tuning and suppression rules - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Run CI and fix linting/format issues Summary of changes and rationale are in-line in commits and files changed. Related: ENG-2471 tracks long-term SLO integration where these metrics will feed cost-optimization pipelines.

release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics with model and route labels; enables per-route cost attribution.
Instrumented KV-cache with hit/miss counters and latency histograms; added cache heatmap panels.
Added tracing spans and baggage for model_id and route to speed up root-cause analysis.
Updated Grafana dashboards and tuned alerting rules to reduce noisy alerts and add burn-rate suppression.
Backwards-compatible metric name normalization: renamed kv_cache_hit_ratio -> kv_cache_hit_rate (non-breaking).
notes: Operational impact: This increases cardinality on some metrics; we added guards and validators to limit explosion. Engineering should monitor metrics ingestion cost for first 2 weeks after roll-out.
Follow-up: wire these metrics into the cost-optimization pipeline (ENG-2471) and add automated alert runbook links in alerts.
Rollout plan: rolled out to staging for 48h then to canary, finally main cluster. Suppression rules help avoid alert storms during canary.
Docs updated at docs/observability/token-kv-metrics.md with sample queries and dashboard screenshots.
